title: Making a large floor cushion from upholstery fabric
subtitle: Sew a box-cushion cover from heavy furnishing fabric and fill with high-resilience foam
excerpt: How to make a large floor cushion from a heavy furnishing or upholstery fabric with a box cushion construction. Covers calculating the cutting layout, sewing the boxing strip, inserting the foam pad, and fitting a zip closure.
sourceNotes: Traditional soft furnishings construction practice. Period upholstery manuals (pre-1928 public domain).

glossaryTerms.definition: A cushion construction with a top panel, a bottom panel, and a narrow side strip (the boxing) that defines the thickness and gives a rectangular, firm profile. The boxing strip is typically 80 to 120 mm wide for a floor cushion and is sewn to the top and bottom panels around all four edges. A zip is set into one face of the boxing strip for cover removal.

Upholstery foam is described by its density (kg per cubic metre: 25 to 40 kg/m3 for seat cushions) and its ILD (Indentation Load Deflection), which is a measure of firmness. A floor cushion needs a medium to firm foam: 35 kg/m3 density and 170 to 220 N (medium-firm) ILD. The CMHR requirement applies to upholstered furniture sold in the UK: UK regulations require CMHR (combustion-modified high-resilience) foam in upholstered furniture made or repaired post-1988.

content.text: for a floor cushion uses a top panel, a bottom panel, and a boxing strip that defines the depth. The foam insert is cut to size and the cover closes with a zip in the boxing strip. You need a sewing machine for the seams; this tutorial covers the cutting and construction logic.

govern how firm the floor cushion will be in use. Order CMHR foam in the finished cushion dimensions (typically 600 x 600 mm or 700 x 700 mm and 75 to 100 mm thick for a comfortable floor cushion) from an upholstery foam supplier who will cut it to size.

Add 15 mm seam allowance to all edges. For a 600 x 600 mm cushion with 75 mm foam: cut two panels at 630 x 630 mm (top and bottom) and four boxing strips at 105 x 630 mm (the boxing height = foam thickness + 30 mm seam allowance). Cut the fabric with the pattern grain running the same direction on both panels. Mark the seam allowance on the wrong side of each piece with tailor's chalk.

Join the four boxing strips end to end with 15 mm seams to form a ring, but leave one seam open to insert the zip. Fit the zip into the open seam following standard zip-setting technique: tack the seam closed first, press open, machine-stitch the zip tape in place either side of the tacked seam, then remove the tacking.
Attach the panels to the boxing

Pin the top panel to one long edge of the boxing ring, right sides together, matching the corners of the panel to the four corner seams of the boxing. Clip the boxing strip at the corners to allow it to turn the right-angle. Machine-stitch around all four sides. Repeat for the bottom panel, leaving the zip accessible. Turn the cover right side out through the open zip.

Compress the foam pad slightly and feed it through the zip opening into the cover. Work the foam into the corners of the cover until the cover face is smooth and the corners are filled. Close the zip.

attrs.symptom: Cover puckers at the corners after inserting the foam
attrs.cause: The boxing strip was not clipped at the corners before sewing to the panels.
attrs.fix: Re-open the seam at the problem corner, snip a small V-notch into the boxing seam allowance at the corner, and re-stitch. The clip allows the boxing to turn the corner without pulling.

attrs.symptom: Foam is difficult to insert through the zip opening
attrs.cause: Zip opening too short relative to the foam dimensions.
attrs.fix: For ease of foam insertion, the zip should run the full length of one boxing side (at minimum). A zip shorter than 400 mm makes foam insertion difficult on a large cushion.
